provenance.source: PR #6168 "ref(batcher): Only flush the bucket that triggered the flush event", squash-merged 2026-05-04; fix commit e17291eea "Do not let a failed flush kill the flusher thread", closes #7138
provenance.note: pre-existing pattern, authored again here: the PR writes SpanBatcher its own _flush_loop (the base class inherited an equally unguarded one), so the reviewed lines are new code that repeats the flaw. The fix wraps both flush calls in capture_internal_exceptions; by then the same lines had moved down one line, and the loop body is byte-identical apart from the guard.

keywords: one failed send permanently ends the background drain
the loop dies on the first failure and nothing drains the queue again
every later item is discarded because nothing drains the accumulator
an unguarded failure stops the worker for good
the send is not guarded, so the first failure ends the flusher
the buffer keeps accepting items that nothing will send
no exception handling means a single failure ends the periodic drain
bugs.note: the daemon loop calls _flush unguarded; the fix's body states the consequence: the thread ends, _ensure_thread still sees the same pid, items keep accumulating to MAX_BEFORE_DROP and are then dropped for the rest of the process lifetime.
